answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by forcing each new identity to post a slowly unlocking bond, then scoring its answers against a similarity ridge of prior submissions. Only after the work sits on a narrow ledge of originality—distinct wording, independent reasoning, and mismatched timing fingerprints—does the protocol forge lasting voting weight. Clustered clones that share phrasing or submit in lockstep have their bonds slashed and their influence frozen, so buying a crowd of empty accounts cannot buy consensus.
